sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Waukegan?
sections.html:
Waukegan owners have three routes: list with an agent, sell without one, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. All three run through the same city paperwork, so the choice mostly comes down to how much repair work, waiting and showing you want to take on.

Waukegan sits on the Lake Michigan shore, about 11 miles south of the Wisconsin line and 37 miles north of downtown Chicago, and it is the most populous city in Lake County. The Census Bureau counted 89,321 people in 2020 and estimates 87,940 for July 1, 2025. With roughly 32,000 households, the city has a large local housing market, and it adds a transfer step that many Illinois towns do not have, covered next.

sections.h2: What is the Waukegan zoning certificate and closing letter?
sections.html:
Waukegan requires a zoning certificate, a life-safety inspection and a closing letter for every transfer of ownership. The city's Closing Letter / Zoning Certificate page says the rule took effect October 16, 2023, under Ordinance 23-0-294.

Applications go in online when the home is listed, and no later than 30 days before closing. A code officer contacts the applicant within five business days of the fee payment to book a minimal code and life-safety inspection. The certificate has to hang where it is fully visible, as near the front entrance as possible, for the whole time the home is on the market.

The city's FAQ is blunt about exceptions: its ordinance lists none, so foreclosure and tax-sale transfers need the same documents. Each parcel number in a sale needs its own closing letter, and a missing number can hold up the closing.

  • Seller side: property details, occupancy status, number of bedrooms or units, MLS number if listed, and the listing agent's contact information.
  • Buyer side, once you have one: a driver's license number for the water account transfer, receipts for any city amounts already settled, and a notarized affidavit.
  • Utility side: call the Water Department at least five business days before closing to schedule the final meter reading (847-360-0535).

The closing letter is issued only after the fees and the final water bill are paid. Any liens on the property are disclosed in the record, and the payoff statements can be settled at closing.

sections.h2: Can I sell my Waukegan house as-is?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's FAQ says a property can sell as-is as long as it has the required zoning certificate inspection and the buyer signs a notarized affidavit. The city does not provide a template, so the affidavit has to carry a date, the buyer's address, phone number and email, a list of the items the buyer takes on from the inspection report, the buyer's signature and the notary's confirmation.

That matters for a fast sale. A cash buyer who agrees to take the inspection items does not hold the closing up for repairs, though the inspection itself still has to happen. Sellers who wait until a contract is signed to apply risk running into the 30-day window.

Illinois also requires a seller of residential property to hand the buyer a completed disclosure report before the contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20). Transfers from an estate fiduciary, by court order or in lieu of foreclosure are among the exempt ones listed in Section 15.

sections.h2: What do Waukegan homes and households look like?
sections.html:
Census figures for 2020 to 2024 describe a city split almost evenly between owners and renters, with values well below the Chicago suburbs to the south.

  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 50.2%
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $190,900
  • Median gross rent: $1,205
  • Households: 32,042, averaging 2.72 people
  • Median household income: $71,919; persons in poverty: 15.3%
  • Residents age 25 or older with a bachelor's degree: 20.9%

The city's roots are industrial. Its harbor, a railroad through town by 1855 and later plants such as a sugar refinery and a barbed-wire maker drew workers from Sweden, Finland, Lithuania and elsewhere. The 2023 annual financial report lists Lake County, Southwire, Vista Medical Center East, Lake Behavioral Hospital and Medline Industries among the largest employers. The city has also pursued a lakefront plan to replace much of the old industrial shoreline with residential and recreational space.

sections.h2: How do Waukegan's schools, roads and transit affect a sale?
sections.html:
Most of Waukegan belongs to Waukegan Community Unit School District 60, which serves about 17,000 students from preschool through grade 12. Waukegan High School runs on two campuses, Brookside for grades 9 and 10 and Washington for grades 11 and 12. Pieces of the city fall inside Gurnee School District 56 with Warren Township High School District 121, and a small section sits in Beach Park District 3 and Zion-Benton District 126, so the district listed on a tax bill is worth checking before you write a listing.

Buyers who commute will look at the Metra Union Pacific North line, the Pace bus hub at Sheridan Road and Washington Street, the Tri-State Tollway and the Amstutz Expressway. The Robert McClory Bike Path crosses the city, and Waukegan National Airport handles general aviation. The lake also tempers the climate, cooling summers and warming winters.

sections.h2: What if the Waukegan house is a rental?
sections.html:
Every rental inside Waukegan city limits needs a license before anyone moves in, according to the city's rental license page. Licenses expire each December 31, the fee is $60 per rented unit, and an application needs planning and zoning pre-approval plus a passed inspection by the Building and Code Department. A code officer reaches out within five business days to schedule it.

Owners with tenants in place should keep the license current while the property is listed and mention the lease terms to the buyer early. Ask the city's License Department how the license is handled when ownership changes.

sections.h2: Where is a Waukegan deed recorded, and what does it need?
sections.html:
Deeds for Waukegan homes go to the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office, which is in the county building at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. Its fee schedule lists a $70 standard document fee and an $82 non-standard fee, and says the only other charges at recording are state and county transfer taxes.

The county's deed packet lists what must be on the document.

  • Signed and dated by the grantor, with a notary acknowledgment
  • The buyer's address, a full legal description and the preparer's name and address
  • A "mail to" address and the name and address for tax bills
  • A completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement

The state tax is set at the rate printed in 35 ILCS 200/31-10: 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. The same packet names six Lake County municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Waukegan is not on that list, though the closing letter described above applies.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix everything the Waukegan inspector finds before I sell?
faqs.a: No. The city allows an as-is sale if the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting the listed items. The inspection still has to be done and the certificate issued, so apply as soon as the house is listed or under agreement.

faqs.q: How much does the Waukegan closing letter process cost?
faqs.a: The city lists $300 at submittal, split into a $150 zoning certificate fee and a $150 closing letter fee. Any other invoiced amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are settled before the letter is issued.

faqs.q: Does a foreclosure or tax-sale transfer skip the Waukegan zoning certificate?
faqs.a: No. The city's FAQ says its ordinance lists no exemptions for transfers such as foreclosure or tax sale, so those transfers also need the application, inspection and closing letter.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Waukegan?
faqs.a: Record it with the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Deeds can be brought in or mailed, and the office can be reached at 847-377-2575 for the current requirements.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale of a Waukegan house take?
faqs.a: The city's own steps set the floor: apply at listing and no later than 30 days before closing, with an inspector calling within five business days of the application. A buyer who accepts the home as-is can close on that schedule, while the contract date and title work set the rest.
